blocks.text: How to Know Your Home Has Poor Indoor Air Quality

Rosenberg Plumbing & Air in San Antonio is aware that it’s difficult to properly ventilate your home, especially in the winter. Different types of pollutants can build up in the air in your house, causing a variety of health issues. Keeping indoor air as clean as possible is important. There are a few signs that you can look for that indicate you have an air quality issue in your home.

Poor air quality could cause your health to deteriorate. If you’ve been sneezing or coughing more often than normal, the air in your home might be the cause. Particulates, including bacteria, viruses, dust mites, and pollen, can impact your lungs, spread disease, and affect your health. Chemical vapors from paints or cleaning products can also circulate around a house if it’s not properly filtered and ventilated.

Having high humidity in your home can lead to a variety of air quality issues. Excess humidity can allow mold to grow, and the spores can become airborne and create problems. If you see condensation on the inside of your windows, you might need to consider getting a dehumidifier for your house.

If you find that your air filters are getting dirty and need to be replaced more often than every three months, there’s a problem. Filters should last for between three and six months before they need to be replaced. Dirt and dust can also build up in the ductwork of your house and lead to problems. Particles can get dislodged from ducts and start circulating in your air.
